caveats: Needs a second config load/reload after the first (e.g. a later admin API request, which runs on its own goroutine, or the dynamic config loader goroutine); admin endpoint must be enabled.
Needs the Go scheduler to delay the first Serve goroutine's initial read until after the second reload's write, which the Go memory model permits but no timing guarantees.
Usage (concurrent reloads against a running server) is judged as stated; the deployment model is UNCONFIRMED.
subclaims.reason: Reload 1 writes the package-global localAdminServer (admin.go:332, declared admin.go:1226 with no guarding lock) and spawns a Serve goroutine that reads the same global (admin.go:342-343) instead of a captured local. Reload 2 runs replaceLocalAdminServer again via run (caddy.go:379) under changeConfig's currentCfgMu (caddy.go:135), but the Serve goroutine never takes that lock, so there is no common lock between its read and reload 2's write. The go statement orders only reload 1's write before the goroutine's start; nothing orders reload 2's write against that read, so a delayed goroutine can read generation 2's server. The goroutines are the generation-1 Serve goroutine (read side) and any reload caller such as an admin API handler goroutine or the dynamic-loader goroutine (caddy.go:489) (write side). Hence the first-generation goroutine can Serve the next generation's server.
